key_insight: A context-aware Markov decision process can tailor Type 2 diabetes follow-up intervals to patient risk, rather than using one fixed schedule for everyone.
clinical_relevance: The approach could help primary care teams space visits more efficiently while keeping closer follow-up for higher-risk patients and those with abnormal labs or recent hospitalization.
method: Used EHR data from 22,154 Type 2 diabetes patients across 10 primary care clinics.
Derived patient contexts by reducing longitudinal health-trajectory variables with PCA and clustering patients using principal components plus patient-level features.
Learned follow-up interval policies with a Contextual Markov Decision Process.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, the CMDP policy lowered expected cumulative cost versus an ADA-like fixed-interval policy, including about 34.8% lower cost in the higher-comorbidity context and 6.4% lower cost in the lower-comorbidity context.
watch_item: The results come from retrospective EHR data and model-based evaluation, so real-world workflow fit, safety, and generalizability need prospective validation.
paper_title: Context-Aware Optimization of Follow-Up Intervals for Type 2 Diabetes Care Using Markov Decision Processes
